events.headline: Wall St ends sharply lower on AI selloff, S&P 500, Dow in correction
events.summary: US equities fell sharply, with the S&P 500 down 3.70% and Nasdaq down 5.28%, as AI valuation concerns intensified after Anthropic's debut. Nvidia declined 13.8%.

events.headline: Fed's Cook says central bank watching AI industry financing
events.summary: Fed Governor Lisa Cook said regulators are monitoring complex, intertwined funding arrangements supporting AI expansion. She highlighted transparency and financial-stability concerns.

events.headline: Signal restricts screenshots to block AI agents from reading messages
events.summary: Signal announced default screenshot restrictions to limit AI assistants' access to private chats. It called for stronger operating-system controls over agents accessing sensitive application data.

events.headline: ABB considers robotics listing if sale to SoftBank fails, sources say
events.summary: ABB is considering listing or otherwise disposing of its robotics unit if a $5.4 billion sale to SoftBank cannot proceed. The parties are exploring restructuring after Chinese objections.

events.headline: Waymo recalls self-driving cars over closed freeway lanes, manual traffic control
events.summary: Waymo disclosed two robotaxi recalls related to closed freeway lanes and manual traffic control, following regulatory scrutiny and a freeway operating pause. One recall remedy was completed while another remained in development.

events.headline: Oracle says OpenAI infrastructure deal is fully funded after final capital raise
events.summary: Oracle said its OpenAI infrastructure contract is fully financed following a final capital raise, responding to investor concerns about AI data-center funding. It reiterated plans for additional gigawatt-scale capacity.

events.headline: States agree to UN talks aiming to regulate 'killer robots' by 2028
events.summary: States agreed to further UN discussions on autonomous weapons rules over two years, without a binding agreement. Major arms-producing nations opposed stronger obligations.
